content.text: {"route":"ready","reason":"The record is adequate to evaluate the merits. It includes statements from Complainant, the alleged harasser (C1), the supervisors (S1, S2, S3, S5), the fact-finder (S4), and the coworker witnesses (C2, C3). It also shows conflicts in the testimony and how the Agency resolved them: it credited some findings, such as the background check, the shared letter, the Sitka exclusion and the slander accusation, and rejected others, such as the lawsuit threat, the Fairbanks comment and the 'gay card' remark. Corroboration from C3 and S1 supports the findings. The Agency's reasoning on severity/pervasiveness and on remedial action can be assessed from the record. Whether the conclusions are legally correct is a separate question from adequacy. The agency's own investigation was cut short, but the record still shows what remedial steps were taken."}
